subject: Clarify billing quantum, prefix reuse, and concession terms
messages:
From: Alicia Romero <alicia@forgehealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Quick Q: billing quantum and prefix reuse?

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Two quick technical/pricing questions the procurement team asked before we can sign:

1) When a single customer request fans out to multiple models (embedding -> reranker -> generator), how do you account tokens? Is it charged per model invocation (i.e., counted separately for each model), or is there some aggregation / de-dupe for shared prompt prefixes?

2) For streaming sessions and heartbeats (our voice transcripts will keep a 60s streaming socket open), how does rounding/minimums apply? We saw reference to a 100-token quantum in the docs — is that global?

3) For long contexts (8k–30k tokens), is there an amortization or different rounding treatment? Our internal legal is worried about small rounding causing large monthly variance.

Can you send 2–3 worked invoice examples for our typical flows (short chat, multi-model pipeline, long context search) so procurement can review?

Appreciate it — copying Markus (finance).

— Alicia
Director of Product
Forge Health

On Thu, Nov 26, 2026 at 10:02 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com> wrote:
To: Alicia Romero <alicia@forgehealth.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Quick Q: billing quantum and prefix reuse?

Hi Alicia —

Thanks, great questions. High level answers first, then I attached a spreadsheet with worked scenarios.

- Multi-model calls: Token consumption is measured per model invocation. We bill tokens consumed by each model instance separately (so embedding + reranker + generator will show up as three line items). That said, we apply prefix reuse credits when identical bytes are passed through the same machine KV cache within the billing window — the net effect is you won’t pay full duplicated prefix every time if requests hit the same cached prefix.

- Rounding/quantum: Default rounding quantum is 100 token-units for hosted accounts. For Dedicated/Private customers we can adjust quantum with commitments. Streaming counts are aggregated per session on a rolling window; we round the aggregated window to the quantum.

- Long contexts (> 16k): For very large contexts we use amortized windowing for stable customers: the runtime will bucket long-context consumption into 1k-token amortized blocks for invoice smoothing, but that requires an explicit commitment or pilot agreement to enable (it’s not on by default).

I attached "redwood_pricing_example_v3.xlsx" with three scenarios: short chat, multi-model pipeline, long-context search. The sheet shows raw token tallies, applied quantum rounding, prefix reuse credit rows, and sample invoice lines.

Next steps: If you can confirm which of the three scenarios most closely matches expected monthly volume and whether you expect streaming or mostly discrete calls, Tessa and I can propose a short pilot concession to reduce variance.

-Vivek
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_pricing_example_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet, ~45KB)

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Romero <alicia@forgehealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick Q: billing quantum and prefix reuse? — proposed pilot concession

Thanks for the heads up, Vivek. Alicia — a few practical concessions we can offer to reduce your procurement team's variance concerns for an initial pilot:

1) Pilot quantum cap: For the pilot period we can cap rounding to 50-token quantum (instead of 100) for all hosted token charges tied to your account.

2) Prefix crediting: We will enable aggressive prefix crediting for identical prompt prefixes within a 24-hour window during the pilot; that will reduce duplicate billing across model calls when you reuse the same system prompt.

3) Temporary discount: 15% off token list rates for the first 90 days of the pilot.

4) Waive minimums: We will waive any monthly minimums for the first 30 days (so you can run the cadence without immediate commit).

Worked examples (high level):
- Short chat (avg prompt 120 tokens, response 80 tokens). Raw tokens: 200 -> quantum 50 -> charged 200 (no rounding up under cap). Monthly estimate (50k calls): ~10M billed tokens -> with 15% discount = charged at 8.5M token-equivalent.
- Multi-model pipeline (embed 300 tokens -> rerank 150 -> generate 900). Raw total per user: 1350 tokens billed across 3 models -> quantum rounds each model to nearest 50, total charged 1350. For 100k such requests monthly -> ~135M billed tokens; with prefix crediting we estimate 8–12% reduction depending on reuse.
- Long-context search (context 12k tokens + 2k generated). We’ll amortize to 1k blocks for the pilot billing demo (not full production amortization) to smooth invoices; example invoice line shows 14 blocks (14k) charged rather than per-call heavy rounding.

I attached a cleaned SOW with pilot terms you can share with legal: "SOW_FH_v2.pdf". If you approve, we’ll apply the pilot settings immediately upon signature.

Next: can you confirm which scenario represents your top load (short chat vs multi-model pipeline vs long-context)? Once we have that I’ll ask Ops to produce a sample invoice for the three example months.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOW_FH_v2.pdf (PDF, ~120KB)

Quick note from legal/accounting side before we finalize pilot language:

- Approvals: The 15% discount and 50-token cap are acceptable for a time-limited pilot, but discount must be tied to a finite pilot window (we typically allow 90 days). Any extension requires written agreement and renewal terms in the SOW.

- Amortization: Full amortized bucket billing for >16k contexts is only available to committed customers (Dedicated/Private) due to execution/QA overhead. The pilot amortization we described is an invoice-smoothing simulation and must be marked as "provisional" on the invoice.

- Audit & reporting: We’ll include a line-item breakdown on each invoice that explicitly calls out prefix credits and rounding adjustments so Forge Health can reconcile to their internal token logs.

I’ll add the above clauses to SOW_FH_v2 and send a redline later today.

— Kimberly Park
Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
